links.reason: Both verses make sila a piece of war equipment (2819 armour of kings, 3074 கவசஞ் சீலம் / வெளிறில்வாள்), but the pairing is one stock metaphor in the same chapter; the shift from guard to weapon is thin.
1564 is the king's reply to the queen's plan (நங்கைதன் மகனைக் காண்டும்), a plot sequence the graph already holds; the maid's message in between is not in either verse.

Both lists spare cows, brahmins and women, but 443 adds துறந்தார், பாலர் and Puram 9 adds the sick and sonless; the epic is a vow, not a code, and 'pedigree' and 'active counterpart' are the note's inference.

98 has a literal goad on a kneeling elephant (தோட்டி கொண்டான்); the verse does nothing to make it an inner discipline, and Tirumular's goad is the five letters. Only the word goad is shared, and the epic sense is flagged uncertain.

3022 bows (வணங்கினான்) at the feet (திருவடி) and Kural 9 condemns the head that does not bow at the feet (தாளை வணங்காத் தலை); a real echo of idea, but the 'crown given its one use' is a flourish and the epic adds nothing the couplet lacks.
396 gives the ascetic's penance against வெஞ்சினம் but nothing in 393 or 396 says the request for a year of no anger comes from that discipline; the note supplies the link between the two.
1845 has படிவ ஒற்றாளர் like the Kural's படிவத்தர் ஒற்று, but the verse does not say whose spies or that the guise is ascetic; 'the epic gains the sense of படிவம்' is unsupported.
196 only describes marriage intimacy (கடி மணக் கிழமை ஓர் கடலின் மிக்கதே); the ruin and the queen's blamelessness come from outside the verse, and Kural 901 does not assume a fault in the wife.
Kural 550 is about punishing the cruel (கொலையிற் கொடியாரை); 54 is about enemies subdued without killing in anger (சீறி). Different cases, so not a rival rule on whether death is a king's work.

1932 is a hell-warden scene of adulterers embracing fiery figures; Siddhar 450 has the pit and loins speaking. Both link lust to ruin, but the 'same fear inside and outside' and 'inner meaning' are the note's reading.

2887 says one word broke the clinging (ஒருசொலே ஏதுவாக), the sense flagged uncertain; the Kural's 'cling to the unclinging one' is not in the verse, so 'the word points to the unclinging one' is imposed.

380 gives two causes, ஊழ்வினை துரத்தலானும் உணர்வு சென்று எறித்தலானும், but never denies grace; Tirumular's தன்செயல் அற்றால் is a different frame. Silence about grace is not an incompatible claim, so 'tension' and 'needs no descent of grace' overstate.

140 gives reasons for the same refusal as Kural 327 (வானுயர் இன்பம் ... மரித்திடும்), so the pairing adds something; but it adds a reason and does not limit the couplet, and no maxim is cited in the verse.

409 foretells that Tivittan will split a lion's mouth within a month (சிங்கம்வாய் பிளந்திடும்) and 769 shows the lion's blood running down the hill (உதிர நீத்தம்); the later verse fulfils the prophecy and shows it only by its trace.

228 is a consolation that denies the dream (கனவின் இயல் மெய் எனும் பெண் மயமோ பெரிதே) and 267 says கனவு எல்லாம் விளைந்த; the reversal is real, but the verse does not show a changed mind or an error, and 269 is not in the packet.

The same bloomed konrai is read as the sign of the season (கடுக்கை ... பருவம் ... மருந்து) and as a fool's mistaken sign (கொன்றை மடவ ... பருவம் வாரா அளவை). The two poems are for different situations, so not a tension.

124 says he forgets his lost land (இழந்ததன் னிலத்தையும் ... நினைத்திலன்) while Kural 539 bids remember the ruined of others; the epic merely fails the rule. The verse does not name the fault the couplet names.

Only the word தவம் is shared: in 467 the city women guess past penance won the hero; in 640 the kings threaten to do penance if they lose, with no stated aim of winning her. 'Penance is the price of a beloved' is not in 640.

637 has the onlookers call her கூற்றம் and bid the suitors run (கொண்டோடிப் போமின்கள் உரைத்தேம்), as Kovalan's song has கொடுங்கூற்றம் in a girl's form (அறியேன் அறிவேனேல் அடையேன்); real figure, real contrast of late and timely warning, but type is a shared image, not qualification, and 637 is flagged uncertain.

The note rests on one reading of ஐயுறான் அணங்கு, which the marker flags as uncertain, and on later plot not in the verse. The pairing with Kural 1081's three-way doubt is attractive but too reading-dependent for the claimed 'first step of absorption'.

1628 has Civakan imagine a wife wasting (நைந்துநைந்து உள்சுட) and 1509 has Kemasari's own cry; the pair is a parallel of lament, and the 'measure his pity against his silence' is irony the Tamil does not state.

377 (கூர் எரி கவரும் போழ்தில் கூடுமோ குறித்த எல்லாம்) and Kural 335 both urge acting before death; the epic's added point that the rare means is wasted on the senses is real, but the 'develops' type and 'gains' are generic.

561 praises kings by high clan (மிக்குயர் குலத்து வேந்தர்) and Naladiyar 195 says birth rank is a word, so they can conflict; but it is the purohit's reported rhetoric, and the founder 'who earned his rank by renouncing' is not in the packet.

529 has Marusi call the king great in forbearance (பொறையினாற் பெரியன்) and Naladiyar 72 praises bearing unfit words (தாரித் திருத்தல் தகுதி), a real connection; but the verse is flagged uncertain and the king's silence is not stated, so the effect on the one borne with is the marker's reading.
links.text_issue: sense flagged uncertain; sentence in lines 1-2 compressed

links.reason: 1630 has the king hide and 1631 has the queen send women to play (மன்னவன் மறைந்த தெண்ணி); the second answers the first, but that is plot sequence, and 'the game she thinks he wants to watch' is not in the text.

255 and 256 share an opening line as decade-mates, but each is a separate poem; 255 says the girl is like (புரையும்) hill goddesses and 256 says she is ஆர் அணங்கினள். Reading the order as a likeness hardening into identity is imposed on a compiler's arrangement.

2235 turns the brides' garlands (மணமாலை) into the ghoul's feast and 803 shows a ghoul dressing from the slain (குடர்க்கண்ணி); same image, but not a tension, and 'cost to the women' is an inference from the garlands.

1097 uses எட்பக அனைத்தும் of attachment and Kural 889 has எட்பக வன்ன of inner enmity; the marker itself notes only two words match, so this is a stock measure, and the Kural's court enmity is not extended to attachment in the epic.

2085 (flagged uncertain) has the lover answer a jealous charge over a gaze (ஒட்டி யான் நோக்கிற்று) and Kural 1320 has the quarrel over a gaze (யாருள்ளி நோக்கினீர்); the painted figure is a real addition, but the construal of line 2 is uncertain.

500 has Maruci open with praise (நண்ணிநின் றிறைஞ்சுவார் அருந்தவஞ் செய்தார்) and Kural 687 praises the envoy who knows protocol; the verse is a courtesy and the pairing illustrates the couplet without the epic adding anything to it.

1953 lists hoarders who die tight-fisted (இறுகு பவர்களும்) and Naladiyar 273 says the hoarder's wealth laughs at him (பொருளும் அவனை நகுமே); both Jain, and the pair adds a worldly and a post-mortem sanction, but the hell setting is not in the verse itself and the link is of the same theme.

The note itself says 'if the two Ezhinis are one'; 396 is Vattaru's Ezhiniyathan and 216 names Selli's Athan Ezhini, joined by the name and the Kosar only. There is no shared image, and the genre-division teaching rests on the identification.

Both use the formula புதுவது அன்று (76 on killing, 192 on சாதலும் புதுவது அன்றே) and the contrast of ends is real, but a shared stock phrase is not a shared image or pattern, and it is not shown that either poem draws on the other.

1625 has the swan's ஊடல் ended by union and Kural 1109 lists ஊடல் உணர்தல் புணர்தல்; the watcher who is parted is a fair addition, but the 'gains' for the epic (the couplet's order explains the swans) are trivial.

1427 has a spell summon Death to finish the world (கூற்றுவன் தன்னைக் கூவி) and Tirumanthiram 176 says nothing of who commands Death, only that thought of the Lord spares one the messengers. The conflict is the note's invention, and 1427 is flagged uncertain.

Both show care for the wounded (818 நெய்க்கழி வைக்கப்பட்டார், வேம்பு-spear and wounds in Nedunalvadai 172-187) but the epic does not develop the Sangam passage; 'grew from presence into provision' is a claimed history, not a link in the Tamil.

2618 has Vijayai say we are scattered by the force of deeds (விடுவினை புடைக்கப் பாறி) and 2815 says all, Indra and monkey, eat their deeds' fruit; the same karma doctrine, but 'no rank of birth can be claimed as refuge' is not said in 2618.

29 describes stored grain that does not shrink (உண்ணிலாங் குலவாமை), which fits தள்ளா விளையுள், but the claim that the poet builds the land from the harvest outward rests on the order of verses not in the packet; the line 1 reading is uncertain.

266 praises the king who guards like his own life and 140 faults a king lacking grace to lower beings; the verses are about different kings and 'the ideal cannot be met by any one virtue' is a generalization the two do not state.

1646 reaches the artificial hill and 1650 has it echo and mock the women (செய்குன்றே ... அசதியாடின்று); the hill as speaker is a shift, but it is the same scene in sequence, and 1650 is flagged uncertain.

1197 is Arkakirti's boast of wrath as arrows (வெகுளிக் காற்றோடு), a speaker's war rhetoric with no doctrine; Kural 305 (சினங்காக்க) is advice, not a rival claim, and the verse does not praise anger as a duty.

1827 has kings console themselves that deeds ripen not as wished (வினையதால் வினையின் றன்மை) and Kural 377 says only the apportioner's apportioning is enjoyed; the doctrine is stated in the verse, and 'equal means' is not in it.

874 has the two rivals sit free of care (எவ்வந் தீர்ந்திருந்தாள்) and the patikam 12 gives their wager over powders; the scene precedes the quarrel, but the 'discord grows from companionship' is the note's reading and the festival bath is not the grove.

1128 addresses the kurava as வாழி நறுங்குரவே and Kural 1111 addresses the anicham as வாழி அனிச்சமே, each against the bride or beloved; the added threat of plucking is real, but it is a shared image, not a qualification, and the epic side gains no new form.
